survivors.claim: In-session Never mind leaves the request card in a shape D6 never renders: the pre-existing withdraw handler sets data-status=resolved and writes the status line "Closed", never adds data-resolution="withdrawn", the D6 sentence or a Put it back control — so until the client reloads, the card they just withdrew shows no way back and the CSS resolved-row rule hides its actions. The reload render (buildWalkPage) is correct; only the in-session path is missing.
survivors.impact: Right after a client takes a request back, the page shows it as simply closed with no way to put it back until they reload — the one-way ratchet this spec closes is still there for the length of the session.

survivors.claim: After sign-off the walk request card and the index closed list still render Put it back, and POST /client/__notes/reopen carries no marks.approved gate — putting a request back after approval reopens the note, and the next walk-page GET materialize retires the derived exclusion row, so the ledger diverges from the dated exclusions.md. Spec-consistent as written (D3 names only exclusion rows and the exclusion route; D6 has no approval condition), so advisory.
survivors.impact: A client can still change the won't-build list after the work is signed off by putting a request back, which is exactly the ledger-versus-contract drift the sign-off cut-off was added to stop.
